pathway.title: STARWOOD PROPERTY TRUST, INC. — Credit Snapshot
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: First, the registrant’s financial risk has risen over the first half of 2026. Total debt on the balance sheet increased to USD 23,694.1 million from USD 22,094.2 million while stockholders’ equity fell to USD 6,499.0 million from USD 6,795.5 million, because dividends declared of USD 357.3 million exceeded net income attributable of USD 58.4 million (Analyst Interpretation on the cause; the amounts are Documentary Fact). The mechanic is simple: a payout above earnings is paid from cash that is then replaced with debt or retained-earnings erosion, so the equity layer that sits beneath every creditor shrinks.

Second, earnings are weak on the filed basis and only adequate on the company basis. The registrant reported net income attributable of USD 6.6 million for the second quarter of 2026 against distributable earnings of USD 151.5 million, a company measure that removes the credit loss provision and unrealized items. Distributable earnings per share of USD 0.78 for the first half trailed dividends declared of USD 0.96 per share, a ratio of 0.81x. The credit implication is that the dividend is not covered by either measure, so the registrant depends on asset resolution and deployment of capital to close the gap (Documentary Fact for the figures; Analyst Interpretation for the reading).

Third, asset quality is the swing factor. The registrant had about USD 947.3 million of loans on nonaccrual at June 30, 2026 by our sum of the amounts the quarterly report states, 36.8% of commercial loans at amortized cost carry loan-to-stabilized-value above 70%, and that bucket holds USD 362.0 million of the USD 406.2 million commercial credit loss allowance. Interest stops accruing on nonaccrual loans, which lowers net interest income and ties up capital that supports the leverage ratio; foreclosures in the first half added USD 347.5 million of owned property. Management says it expects to resolve nearly USD 900 million of underperforming assets by year end or shortly after, which is Management Language and not evidence of resolution.

Fourth, funding structure is a strength with a catch. Most debt is matched-term secured funding, 68% of repurchase agreements do not permit valuation adjustments based on capital market events, and the registrant refinanced USD 1,100.0 million of unsecured notes in the quarter and the month after. The catch is rank and opacity: USD 18,932.4 million of secured and securitized financing is secured on pledged assets, corporate term loans of USD 2,533.1 million are secured on subsidiary equity, and the USD 4,930.8 million of unsecured notes rank behind both on those assets. Covenant levels are not supplied, so headroom is Not calculable even though the registrant states compliance.

Fifth, governance adds a monitoring item. The registrant is externally managed by an affiliate of its sponsor, the management agreement was not negotiated at arm’s length and carries a termination fee of three times average annual fees, and several loans were made to borrowers connected to affiliates of the manager with board approval. The mechanic is weaker creditor control rather than an observed loss; no creditor-adverse action was found in the pages read (Insufficient Information on the documents).

runs.text: Strengths. The registrant has proven access to secured and unsecured markets (Documentary Fact): 2025 saw a USD 534.4 million share issuance, USD 1,550.0 million of new senior notes and a USD 700.0 million term loan, and 2026 added a USD 600.0 million note, a USD 275.0 million term loan upsizing and several securitizations, which reduces refinancing risk. The funding is mostly matched to assets, with the next four quarters of projected principal inflows exceeding projected required financing repayments by USD 785.1 million (Documentary Fact, company projection), so asset repayments fund most secured maturities. The platform is diversified across commercial lending, infrastructure lending, owned property and servicing, with a named special servicing portfolio of USD 93.6 billion (Documentary Fact), which gives several earnings sources. The unsecured note stack is long-dated after July 2026: the first unsecured maturity is the USD 380.8 million convertible notes in July 2027 (Analyst Interpretation from the maturity table). About 79% of unsecured principal is swapped to floating rates, which matches floating-rate assets but adds hedge counterparty exposure (Analyst Interpretation).

Weaknesses. Leverage has risen at each balance sheet date in the financial base, to 3.65x total debt to stockholders’ equity (Documentary Fact for the inputs, calculated ratio). Earnings do not cover the dividend, and GAAP interest cover is 1.22x on a trailing basis (Analyst Interpretation, includes fair value and consolidated VIE items). Nonaccrual loans of about USD 947.3 million and an office share of 17.6% of the commercial portfolio concentrate asset-quality risk (Documentary Fact; sum calculated). The structure is complex: GAAP assets include USD 30,868.1 million of securitization VIE assets, and the registrant states it is not obligated to provide financial support to those VIEs, so ratios on different perimeters are not comparable (Documentary Fact). Governance is the sponsor’s: manager fees, a termination fee and related-party loans reduce creditor control (Documentary Fact; creditor effect is Analyst Interpretation). The most important evidence is missing: governing debt documents, covenant levels, guarantor terms and ratings are not supplied (Insufficient Information), and no filing covers the period after the second quarter of 2026.

runs.text: The registrant’s transaction history in the sources is a sequence of financings and one acquisition, not a single event. In the second quarter of 2026 it issued 600.0 million dollars of 6.125% Senior Notes due June 2031 on May 26, 2026 and swapped them to a floating rate of SOFR plus 2.22%, with a make-whole call before December 1, 2030 (10-Q Q2 2026 page:57; page:105). In May 2026 it amended its term loan facility due September 2032, raising it by 275.0 million dollars to 971.5 million dollars and cutting the spread by 25 basis points (10-Q Q2 2026 page:105). In April 2026 it entered a one-billion-dollar revolving warehouse facility for Fundamental’s net lease acquisitions, of which 500.0 million dollars is committed and 500.0 million dollars uncommitted, with a five-year term and a rate of SOFR plus 1.55% (10-Q Q2 2026 page:50). In the first quarter of 2026 it refinanced infrastructure loans through the Starwood 2026-SIF7 CLO in January and refinanced Fundamental net lease properties through ABS FI Series 2026-1 in March with 466.4 million dollars of third party financing at a weighted average fixed rate of 5.06% (10-Q Q2 2026 page:107). The use of proceeds is stated for the May 2026 notes: the 10-Q says the 2026 Senior Notes were repaid with proceeds of the issuance in the second quarter (10-Q Q2 2026 page:57). Status of these items is completed as of June 30, 2026.

Subsequent events after June 30, 2026, as stated in the Q2 2026 quarterly report (10-Q Q2 2026 page:101): in July 2026 the registrant issued 500.0 million dollars of 5.875% Senior Notes due August 15, 2029 and used the proceeds to redeem the 500.0 million dollars of 2027 Senior Notes due January 15, 2027, recognising a derivative loss of 6.3 million dollars on the hedge unwind; it repaid the 400.0 million dollars of 2026 Senior Notes at maturity; it refinanced Fundamental net lease properties through ABS FI Series 2026-2 with 321.0 million dollars of third party financing at a weighted average fixed rate of 5.47%; it redeemed at par the third party financing of the STWD 2021-FL2 and STWD 2022-FL3 CLOs and amended a commercial credit facility, increasing its maximum size by 1.2 billion dollars to 3.0 billion dollars. These are subsequent events and are not folded into the June 30, 2026 balance sheet or the maturity table; the financial base handoff shows the unsecured-note pro forma separately.

In 2025 the principal transaction was the acquisition of Fundamental Income Properties, LLC by merger on July 23, 2025 for about 2.2 billion dollars inclusive of 1.3 billion dollars of assumed indebtedness; the merger was treated as an asset acquisition, with debt assumed of 878.3 million dollars of ABS financing and 400.6 million dollars of revolving secured financing (10-K FY2025 page:9; page:188). The 2025 funding included 27.1 million shares of common stock for proceeds of 534.4 million dollars, a 700.0 million dollar seven-year term loan at SOFR plus 2.25%, and unsecured notes of 500.0 million dollars at 6.50% due 2030 in April, 500.0 million dollars at 5.25% due 2028 in October and 550.0 million dollars at 5.75% due 2031 in October (10-K FY2025 page:103). Management called 2025 a year of record capital transactions (Release YE2025 page:2), which is Management Language; the filed amounts above are the documentary basis.

Capital returns are part of the transaction record: in February 2026 the board authorised repurchases of up to 400.0 million dollars of common shares and convertible notes over one year, with 370.1 million dollars of capacity remaining at June 30, 2026 after 29.9 million dollars of share repurchases in the first half (10-Q Q2 2026 page:147). A quarterly dividend of 0.48 dollars a share continued; the financial base handoff shows distributable earnings per share below that level in the first half of 2026. Whether the buyback and dividend interact with financial covenants cannot be tested because covenant levels are not supplied.

fields.value: Starwood Property Trust, Inc. is a Maryland real estate investment trust that lends against commercial and residential real estate and infrastructure, owns property through its Property Segment, and services and invests in commercial mortgage securities. It is a holding company run through wholly-owned subsidiaries and is externally managed by SPT Management, LLC, which is controlled by its chairman and chief executive and is an affiliate of Starwood Capital Group. For a creditor the central business facts are that funding is mostly secured and asset-level, that unsecured notes are issued at the registrant level and swapped to floating rates, that the July 2025 acquisition of Fundamental moved the company toward owned, long-lease net lease property, and that the manager’s fee arrangements and related-party loans make governance a monitoring topic. The most important gap is documentary: the indentures, credit agreements and the management agreement are not supplied, so legal capacity (what the documents permit) cannot be separated from willingness (what was done) and feasibility (liquidity and market access). No filing after the second quarter of 2026 is supplied, so transaction history after August 6, 2026 is unknown, not absent.

fields.value: The registrant’s transaction history in the sources is a sequence of financings and one acquisition, not a single event. In the second quarter of 2026 it issued 600.0 million dollars of 6.125% Senior Notes due June 2031 on May 26, 2026 and swapped them to a floating rate of SOFR plus 2.22%, with a make-whole call before December 1, 2030 (10-Q Q2 2026 page:57; page:105). In May 2026 it amended its term loan facility due September 2032, raising it by 275.0 million dollars to 971.5 million dollars and cutting the spread by 25 basis points (10-Q Q2 2026 page:105). In April 2026 it entered a one-billion-dollar revolving warehouse facility for Fundamental’s net lease acquisitions, of which 500.0 million dollars is committed and 500.0 million dollars uncommitted, with a five-year term and a rate of SOFR plus 1.55% (10-Q Q2 2026 page:50). In the first quarter of 2026 it refinanced infrastructure loans through the Starwood 2026-SIF7 CLO in January and refinanced Fundamental net lease properties through ABS FI Series 2026-1 in March with 466.4 million dollars of third party financing at a weighted average fixed rate of 5.06% (10-Q Q2 2026 page:107). The use of proceeds is stated for the May 2026 notes: the 10-Q says the 2026 Senior Notes were repaid with proceeds of the issuance in the second quarter (10-Q Q2 2026 page:57). Status of these items is completed as of June 30, 2026.

fields.value: 1. Manager economics and control. Evidence: the base fee is a percentage of defined stockholders’ equity, the incentive fee needs core earnings above a hurdle, and removal triggers a fee of three times the average annual fees (10-K FY2025 pages 26, 237 and 238). Risk mechanic: the base fee does not fall with asset quality or leverage, and the cost of removal reduces the board’s practical ability to change manager if performance weakens. Credit implication: manager alignment with creditors rests on board oversight rather than on contract terms the creditor can observe; monitoring posture should track fees against earnings, and the credit module should record that the management agreement itself is not supplied. Counter-evidence: no incentive fee was incurred in the second quarter of 2026, and half of any incentive fee is paid in shares.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 2. Related-party lending. Evidence: ten board-approved related-party loan transactions, including loans where the registrant lacks certain co-lender consent rights because of an affiliate’s interest (10-Q Q2 2026 page:69). Risk mechanic: a lender to affiliate-connected borrowers may have weaker control in a workout and faces a conflict between the manager’s affiliates and the registrant. Credit implication: concentration to affiliate-connected borrowers is an open monitoring item; the sources give transaction-level amounts but no aggregate, so no exposure conclusion is drawn.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 3. Funding access and maturity management. Evidence: regular unsecured, term loan, CLO and ABS financings in 2025 and 2026, with the July 2026 notes replacing the 2026 and January 2027 maturities (10-Q Q2 2026 page:101). Risk mechanic: refinancing earlier than maturity extends the maturity profile and reduces reliance on a single market, but the registrant’s funding is mostly secured on pledged assets, and access depends on collateral values. Credit implication: refinancing risk in the near term is reduced for unsecured debt; the credit module should test secured maturities, availability and covenant headroom. Counter-evidence: leverage in the financial base rose over the same period.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 4. Shift toward owned net lease property. Evidence: Fundamental’s 100.0% occupancy and 16.8 year weighted remaining lease term (10-Q Q2 2026 page:141) and ABS debt service coverage covenants (10-Q Q2 2026 page:52). Risk mechanic: long contracted rents add revenue visibility, while ABS debt at special purpose vehicles is secured on those properties and is structurally ahead of unsecured claims on them; covenants at the vehicle can restrict cash release. Credit implication: property income is more predictable, but cash reaching the registrant depends on vehicle-level tests whose levels are not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Starwood Property Trust, Inc. is an adequately funded real estate lender whose credit quality is weakening at the margin. Its strongest support is funding access: it issued USD 600.0 million of unsecured notes in May 2026 and USD 500.0 million in July 2026, cleared its 2026 and January 2027 maturities, and has USD 1,399.0 million of lender-approved undrawn secured capacity. Its weakest point is earnings against leverage: second quarter 2026 net income attributable was USD 6.6 million, distributable earnings per share trailed the dividend, and debt to stockholders’ equity rose to 3.65x from 3.25x, with nonaccrual loans near USD 947.3 million. Resolution of those loans and continued secured funding decide the outcome.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: First, the registrant’s financial risk has risen over the first half of 2026. Total debt on the balance sheet increased to USD 23,694.1 million from USD 22,094.2 million while stockholders’ equity fell to USD 6,499.0 million from USD 6,795.5 million, because dividends declared of USD 357.3 million exceeded net income attributable of USD 58.4 million (Analyst Interpretation on the cause; the amounts are Documentary Fact). The mechanic is simple: a payout above earnings is paid from cash that is then replaced with debt or retained-earnings erosion, so the equity layer that sits beneath every creditor shrinks.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Second, earnings are weak on the filed basis and only adequate on the company basis. The registrant reported net income attributable of USD 6.6 million for the second quarter of 2026 against distributable earnings of USD 151.5 million, a company measure that removes the credit loss provision and unrealized items. Distributable earnings per share of USD 0.78 for the first half trailed dividends declared of USD 0.96 per share, a ratio of 0.81x. The credit implication is that the dividend is not covered by either measure, so the registrant depends on asset resolution and deployment of capital to close the gap (Documentary Fact for the figures; Analyst Interpretation for the reading).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Third, asset quality is the swing factor. The registrant had about USD 947.3 million of loans on nonaccrual at June 30, 2026 by our sum of the amounts the quarterly report states, 36.8% of commercial loans at amortized cost carry loan-to-stabilized-value above 70%, and that bucket holds USD 362.0 million of the USD 406.2 million commercial credit loss allowance. Interest stops accruing on nonaccrual loans, which lowers net interest income and ties up capital that supports the leverage ratio; foreclosures in the first half added USD 347.5 million of owned property. Management says it expects to resolve nearly USD 900 million of underperforming assets by year end or shortly after, which is Management Language and not evidence of resolution.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fourth, funding structure is a strength with a catch. Most debt is matched-term secured funding, 68% of repurchase agreements do not permit valuation adjustments based on capital market events, and the registrant refinanced USD 1,100.0 million of unsecured notes in the quarter and the month after. The catch is rank and opacity: USD 18,932.4 million of secured and securitized financing is secured on pledged assets, corporate term loans of USD 2,533.1 million are secured on subsidiary equity, and the USD 4,930.8 million of unsecured notes rank behind both on those assets. Covenant levels are not supplied, so headroom is Not calculable even though the registrant states compliance.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fifth, governance adds a monitoring item. The registrant is externally managed by an affiliate of its sponsor, the management agreement was not negotiated at arm’s length and carries a termination fee of three times average annual fees, and several loans were made to borrowers connected to affiliates of the manager with board approval. The mechanic is weaker creditor control rather than an observed loss; no creditor-adverse action was found in the pages read (Insufficient Information on the documents).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths. The registrant has proven access to secured and unsecured markets (Documentary Fact): 2025 saw a USD 534.4 million share issuance, USD 1,550.0 million of new senior notes and a USD 700.0 million term loan, and 2026 added a USD 600.0 million note, a USD 275.0 million term loan upsizing and several securitizations, which reduces refinancing risk. The funding is mostly matched to assets, with the next four quarters of projected principal inflows exceeding projected required financing repayments by USD 785.1 million (Documentary Fact, company projection), so asset repayments fund most secured maturities. The platform is diversified across commercial lending, infrastructure lending, owned property and servicing, with a named special servicing portfolio of USD 93.6 billion (Documentary Fact), which gives several earnings sources. The unsecured note stack is long-dated after July 2026: the first unsecured maturity is the USD 380.8 million convertible notes in July 2027 (Analyst Interpretation from the maturity table). About 79% of unsecured principal is swapped to floating rates, which matches floating-rate assets but adds hedge counterparty exposure (Analyst Interpretation).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weaknesses. Leverage has risen at each balance sheet date in the financial base, to 3.65x total debt to stockholders’ equity (Documentary Fact for the inputs, calculated ratio). Earnings do not cover the dividend, and GAAP interest cover is 1.22x on a trailing basis (Analyst Interpretation, includes fair value and consolidated VIE items). Nonaccrual loans of about USD 947.3 million and an office share of 17.6% of the commercial portfolio concentrate asset-quality risk (Documentary Fact; sum calculated). The structure is complex: GAAP assets include USD 30,868.1 million of securitization VIE assets, and the registrant states it is not obligated to provide financial support to those VIEs, so ratios on different perimeters are not comparable (Documentary Fact). Governance is the sponsor’s: manager fees, a termination fee and related-party loans reduce creditor control (Documentary Fact; creditor effect is Analyst Interpretation). The most important evidence is missing: governing debt documents, covenant levels, guarantor terms and ratings are not supplied (Insufficient Information), and no filing covers the period after the second quarter of 2026.

The company’s own four-quarter overhang table shows projected principal inflows of USD 5,063.7 million (USD 4,937.6 million on loans and held-to-maturity securities plus USD 126.2 million on CMBS and RMBS) against projected required financing repayments of USD 4,278.7 million, a net USD 785.1 million, positive in each of the four quarters (10-Q Q2 2026 page:146); it excludes unsecured notes and is a management projection.

The April 2026 Fundamental warehouse facility has USD 500.0 million committed and USD 500.0 million uncommitted, but its drawn balance is not itemised. Facilities with current maturities inside twelve months of June 30, 2026 include property financing from July 2026, commercial repurchase lines from August 2026, CMBS and RMBS lines from November 2026, conduit lines from December 2026, commercial financing facilities from January 2027 and residential repurchase lines from February 2027, each with later extended maturities subject to conditions (10-Q Q2 2026 pages 142 and 143).
